chunks: Take the pebbles of the Jamarat from Jamʿ. If you wish, you may take them from your provisions at Mina. Do not take from the pebbles of the Jamarat that have already been thrown, and do not break the stones as the common people do. There is no harm in taking the pebbles of the Jamarat from wherever you wish within the Haram, except from al-Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Khayf. They should be speckled, dark, like a fingertip, or like the pebbles used for khadhf; wash them while they are seventy pebbles, tie them in the corner of your garment, and keep them محفوظ.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sacred Precinct around Makkah from which collection is generally permitted.
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ: The Sacred Mosque, excluded here as a place from which the pebbles should not be taken.
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jamʿ, i.e. Muzdalifah, the place from which the pebbles are preferably collected.
key_terms.حَصَى الْجِمَارِ: The pebbles used for the rite of stoning the Jamarat during hajj.
key_terms.حَصَى الْخَذْفِ: Small pebbles of the size used for flicking or slinging, indicating the proper size.
key_terms.سَبْعُونَ حَصَاةً: Seventy pebbles, the required total number to be prepared.
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الْخَيْفِ: Masjid al-Khayf, also excluded here as a place for collecting the pebbles.

ai.seo_question: From where should the pebbles for the Jamarat be collected, and what conditions should they meet?
ai.summary: This passage sets out fiqh rulings for selecting the pebbles used in the rite of stoning during hajj. It specifies their place of collection, forbids using previously thrown or artificially broken stones, and describes their preferred size, number, and handling.
